1 Foot Apart, Never Distant

A little something from me, before the party gets loud.

We've been friends since school. Somewhere along the way we built the strangest rhythm — two years of not talking a single word, then two years of talking every single day, on repeat, like clockwork neither of us ever planned. And somehow it never once felt broken.

You've always been my magical genie — the one who shows up right when my life is falling apart, no summons needed, just there. Every picture we've ever taken together (with you looming a full foot above me in every single one), every car ride, every deep talk at odd hours, every bit of motivation you handed me without making it a big deal, every difficult time you simply refused to let me sit through alone — I'm keeping all of it.

I never once got to celebrate your birthday with you, all these years. That still bugs me. And now, sending you off into married life honestly feels like sending you off to a different country — like the genie's about to have his own house for the first time, and I'm so happy and so unready for it at once.

I'm so glad you found Rithika, and I'm even happier that you're the one getting married first. I'm the only person on earth who's ever understood your typos without asking "wait what," and somehow you're the one who reads exactly what I'm feeling before I've said a word about it. Our gym dates were never just about the gym. Thank you for dragging me into starting in the first place, and for every unsolicited skincare lecture you've ever given me — you've genuinely brought out the best version of me, more than you probably know.

We've always picked outfits for each other before anything else, and hyped each other up over the smallest wins like they were huge ones. I used to love your chubby phase enough to poke your belly every single time I saw you, no warning, no shame, and you never once complained. We did face treatments together like it was a scheduled ritual. And no matter how many pictures we'd already sent each other that day, we'd still hold off and wait to show each other the actual look in person, just to watch each other's face light up first.

I used to call you "Mithunu." Somewhere along the way it turned into "Kannu," and it just stuck. Kannu means eyes — and that's exactly what it's always been, because every single time I see you, mine light up. Still do.

So tonight, before Thalaivar becomes a husband — this one's for every version of us that got us here.

— Indu

Chapters of Us

If this were a film, here's how the reel would run.

Chapter 1 — School Days

Where it all started, long before either of us had any idea it would last this long.

Chapter 2 — The Silence

Two years of nothing. No fight, no explanation needed, none ever given.

Chapter 3 — The Return

Back like no time had passed at all. Then two years straight of everything, all over again.

Chapter 4 — The Gym Era

Sweat, unsolicited skincare advice, and someone finally showing up when they said they would.

Chapter 5 — The Genie Years

Every distress call answered. Every difficult night sat through, no summons needed.

Chapter 6 — The Last Ride

Thalaivar exits bachelorhood. Seyalalar stays on duty, as always.
